html:
The Sateré-Mawé are a Tupian people of the middle Amazon in Brazil, living between the Madeira and Tapajós rivers on the border of Amazonas and Pará, around the town of Maués.

They are the people who first cultivated guaraná, a forest vine whose caffeine-rich seeds they roast, pound and grate into a drink taken every day; the plant is now grown widely for soft drinks. Young men prove their courage in the tucandeira ritual, wearing gloves woven full of stinging bullet ants. Missionaries and traders reached them from the 1600s onward. Today they live on the Andirá-Marau Indigenous Land, in the Amazon rainforest. Their neighbours to the south are the Munduruku.
sum: The Sateré-Mawé are a Tupian people of the middle Amazon in Brazil, living between the Madeira and Tapajós rivers on the border of Amazonas and Pará, around the town of Maués.
